title: Includes a Linux kernel header
message: <linux/...> and <asm/...> are Linux kernel uapi headers. The QNX SDP 8.0 (build 141) ships no linux/, asm/ or asm-generic/ directory: every such include fails to compile (checked for 21 common ones with qcc on x86_64 and aarch64le). Many uses are trivial (linux/limits.h, linux/types.h can be replaced by POSIX headers); device-ioctl headers are not.
remedy: Replace each use with the POSIX/QNX equivalent of what the header supplied (types, constants). If it is a device ioctl header, the device needs a QNX resource-manager interface (devctl) instead.
verify: Checked on SDP 8.0 build 141: no linux/ or asm/ include directory exists. Other SDP versions: verify against SDP.

title: Includes a Linux-specific <sys/...> header
message: This glibc/Linux <sys/...> header is not in the QNX 8.0 SDP for most of the names this rule matches (sys/epoll.h, eventfd.h, signalfd.h, timerfd.h, prctl.h, sendfile.h, sysinfo.h, fanotify.h do not exist in build 141). Two exceptions are present: <sys/inotify.h> (needs -lfsnotify) and <sys/auxv.h> (exists, but getauxval is not declared).
remedy: Remove the include together with the calls it supports (see the per-API findings), or guard it with #if defined(__linux__) and add a __QNXNTO__ branch.
verify: Per-header result from SDP 8.0 build 141 (qcc include probe). Other SDP versions: verify against SDP.

present.message: This header exists in SDP 8.0 build 141. Whether the calls it normally declares exist is decided by the per-API findings (sys/inotify.h: yes, with -lfsnotify; sys/auxv.h: no getauxval).

title: Includes a Linux-only system library header
message: systemd, udev, D-Bus, SELinux, libcap and libnl are Linux system services/libraries; they are not part of a stock QNX image.
remedy: Isolate behind an interface and provide a QNX implementation (service start-up via the QNX service launcher, device discovery via resource managers), or disable the feature on QNX.
verify: verify against SDP: a port of the library may exist (qnx-ports); check before rewriting.

title: epoll event loop
message: epoll does not exist on QNX 8.0: no <sys/epoll.h>, no epoll_* symbol in any SDP library, no EPOLL* macro (checked on SDP 8.0 build 141, x86_64 and aarch64le). kqueue/kevent are NOT a way out: <sys/event.h> is not shipped to user code (the BSD event headers sit only in the io-sock driver include tree) and no library exports kqueue or kevent.
remedy: Port the loop to poll(), ppoll() or select()/pselect() (all four exist in SDP 8.0). ionotify() with SIGEV_PULSE is native QNX (present in the SDP) but only works for resource managers that implement the notify handler for that fd; do not assume it covers sockets. For a pure resource-manager design use the dispatch_* framework (present).
verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141 (header probe, symbol probe, link probe).

title: inotify file watching
message: inotify EXISTS on QNX 8.0: <sys/inotify.h> is in the SDP and libfsnotify exports inotify_init/init1/add_watch/rm_watch (SDP 8.0 build 141: compile and link succeed with -lfsnotify). The IN_* masks (including IN_ACCESS, IN_ATTRIB, IN_CLOSE_WRITE, IN_CREATE, IN_DELETE, IN_MODIFY, IN_MOVED_FROM/TO) and struct inotify_event are defined.
remedy: Add -lfsnotify to the link line (on QNX only) and test the event masks the code relies on: only the compile and link steps were verified, no program was run on a QNX target, so semantic parity with Linux inotify (recursive watches, rename events, filesystem coverage) is unchecked. Keep a stat() polling fallback until it has run on the target.
verify: Compile/link verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; runtime behaviour not tested.

present.message: inotify exists in the SDP (sys/inotify.h, libfsnotify). Needs -lfsnotify; runtime semantics not tested.

title: eventfd
message: eventfd is a Linux file-descriptor wake-up primitive. It does not exist on QNX 8.0 (no <sys/eventfd.h>, no eventfd symbol, no EFD_* macro in SDP 8.0 build 141).
remedy: Use a pipe() or socketpair() pair when the consumer needs a pollable fd; use a pulse (MsgSendPulse / SIGEV_PULSE) when the consumer already sits in MsgReceive.
verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: signalfd
message: signalfd turns signals into a readable fd. It does not exist on QNX 8.0 (no <sys/signalfd.h>, no signalfd symbol in SDP 8.0 build 141).
remedy: Block the signals and consume them in a dedicated thread with sigwaitinfo(), forwarding to the event loop by pipe or pulse.

positive:
fd = signalfd(-1, &mask, SFD_CLOEXEC);
struct signalfd_siginfo si;

verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: timerfd
message: timerfd is Linux-only. It does not exist on QNX 8.0 (no <sys/timerfd.h>, no timerfd_* symbol, no TFD_* macro in SDP 8.0 build 141).
remedy: Use timer_create() with a SIGEV_PULSE sigevent so the timer fires into your channel, or a thread blocked in clock_nanosleep().

positive:
int t = timerfd_create(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, TFD_NONBLOCK);
timerfd_settime(t, 0, &its, NULL);

verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: sendfile/splice zero-copy calls
message: Linux zero-copy file transfer calls. On SDP 8.0 build 141: splice, tee, vmsplice, copy_file_range and sendfile64 are not declared. sendfile() is declared in <sys/socket.h> with the BSD signature (7 arguments) but no SDP library exports it: linking fails (also with -lsocket). A same-named Linux call would not have compiled against that prototype anyway.
remedy: Fall back to a read()/write() loop (or mmap + write) behind a small helper; add a platform fast path only if profiling demands it.
verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (header, symbol and link probes).

title: accept4
message: accept4() exists on QNX 8.0: declared in <sys/socket.h>, and it links when -lsocket is on the link line (SDP 8.0 build 141: it does not link with the default libraries). It is not in POSIX.1-2017, so a strict-POSIX build may need the BSD/QNX feature macros.
remedy: Link with -lsocket (QNX only). Runtime behaviour of the flags argument was not tested on a target.
verify: Compile/link verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; not run.

present.message: accept4 exists in the SDP; it needs -lsocket.

title: SOCK_NONBLOCK / SOCK_CLOEXEC type flags
message: SOCK_NONBLOCK / SOCK_CLOEXEC or-ed into the socket type: both are defined in <sys/socket.h> on SDP 8.0 build 141 (compile probe passes), so this is not a gap. Runtime behaviour not tested.
remedy: Nothing to change for compilation; socket calls need -lsocket on the link line. If a target test shows the flags are ignored, fall back to fcntl().
verify: Compile verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; not run.

title: pipe2 / dup3
message: On SDP 8.0 build 141 pipe2() is declared in <unistd.h> and exists in libc; dup3() is not declared and no library exports it.
remedy: pipe2: nothing to change. dup3: use dup2() then fcntl(fd, F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC) (mind the small race window if other threads fork).
verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141: pipe2 present, dup3 absent.

title: MSG_NOSIGNAL
message: MSG_NOSIGNAL is defined on QNX 8.0 (SDP 8.0 build 141, <sys/socket.h>), so this is not a gap.
remedy: Nothing to change for compilation. Keeping signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) is harmless; SO_NOSIGPIPE is also defined on this SDP.
verify: Compile verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; not run.

title: prctl
message: prctl is a Linux process-control multiplexer. It does not exist on QNX 8.0 (no <sys/prctl.h>, no prctl symbol, no PR_* macro in SDP 8.0 build 141).
remedy: Map each option individually: PR_SET_NAME -> pthread_setname_np() (declared and exported in SDP 8.0 build 141; so is pthread_getname_np); PR_SET_PDEATHSIG -> a parent-liveness check; PR_SET_DUMPABLE -> drop (no QNX analogue is known). PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS: dropping the call silently weakens a sandbox; re-implement with procmgr abilities (procmgr_ability() and the PROCMGR_AID_* / PROCMGR_ADN_* / PROCMGR_AOP_* constants in <sys/procmgr.h>, present in SDP 8.0 build 141; which abilities to drop is design work) or accept the loss explicitly and write it down.
verify: Absence of prctl and PR_* verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (probes); pthread_setname_np, procmgr_ability and the PROCMGR_* constants verified present by probe. Which abilities replace NO_NEW_PRIVS, and the name-length limit of pthread_setname_np, are not verified.

title: CPU affinity (sched_setaffinity & friends)
message: Linux affinity API. On SDP 8.0 build 141 sched_setaffinity, sched_getaffinity, pthread_setaffinity_np, pthread_getaffinity_np, pthread_attr_setaffinity_np, cpu_set_t and the CPU_* macros are all missing (the CPU_* set macros exist only in the io-sock driver headers).
remedy: Use ThreadCtl(_NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK, &mask) for the calling thread (ThreadCtl and _NTO_TCTL_RUNMASK are present in SDP 8.0 build 141; the argument layout and the privilege needed were not tested). Semantics are narrower: Linux sched_setaffinity(pid, ...) can target another process or thread, the runmask call applies to the calling thread, so per-pid callers need restructuring.
verify: Absence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; ThreadCtl usage not run.

title: memfd_create
message: Anonymous in-memory file descriptors are Linux-only. On SDP 8.0 build 141 memfd_create and MFD_* are not available to user code (the names occur only in io-sock driver headers).
remedy: Closest analogue: shm_open(SHM_ANON, O_RDWR, 0600) then ftruncate()+mmap(): shm_open and SHM_ANON are both present in SDP 8.0 build 141 (compile probe; the unnamed-object behaviour was not run). Fallback: shm_open() with a unique name followed by an immediate shm_unlink(), which leaves a short window where the name is visible (racy).
verify: Absence and symbol presence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; SHM_ANON behaviour not run.

title: getrandom
message: getrandom is a Linux syscall wrapper. On SDP 8.0 build 141 getrandom is not declared and GRND_* do not exist; getentropy is not declared either (an unrelated library, libunbound, exports a private symbol of that name, so a call without a prototype would link to the wrong thing). arc4random is not available to user code.
remedy: Read from /dev/urandom with a helper that handles short reads, EINTR and open failure. /dev/urandom exists only while QNX's random service (the `random` resource manager) is running: an image built with mkqnximage starts it (its startup script runs `random` and waits for /dev/random), but a minimal or custom image may not, so add it to the image's startup and treat a failed open as a hard error. <entropy.h> in the SDP is the QNX entropy-source interface (entropy_return_status/entropy_sleep exist in the header; entropy_return_status does not link by default), not a getrandom replacement.
verify: Absence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141. That a default mkqnximage image starts `random` was read from its generated startup script; that /dev/urandom (not only /dev/random) appears was not run on a target.

title: Raw Linux syscall()
message: Linux syscall numbers (SYS_*, __NR_*) have no meaning on QNX, and syscall() is not declared in the SDP (build 141). gettid() DOES exist natively (declared in <sys/process.h>, exported by libc), so SYS_gettid callers need only the call.
remedy: Replace each call with the libc/POSIX function it wraps. gettid(): include <sys/process.h> and call gettid() (present; whether the number is a Linux-style kernel tid was not checked: use it as a numeric id for logging, not for kernel interfaces). Do not substitute pthread_self() (opaque handle). futex has no mechanical replacement (not declared; no library exports it): redesign onto pthread mutex/condvar.
verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141: syscall and futex absent, gettid present.

title: clone/unshare/setns namespaces
message: Linux process/namespace primitives. On SDP 8.0 build 141 clone, unshare, setns and the CLONE_* flags are not available to user code; there is no namespace equivalent.
remedy: Use fork()/posix_spawn() and pthreads. Isolation features must be redesigned with QNX process management (no namespace equivalent is assumed).

negative: static int clone(int a) { return a; }

verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: AF_NETLINK sockets
message: netlink is Linux-only. On SDP 8.0 build 141 AF_NETLINK/PF_NETLINK are defined as socket-family numbers (BSD header heritage) but struct sockaddr_nl and NETLINK_* are not, so a netlink socket cannot be used. Whether socket(AF_NETLINK) is accepted at run time was not tested.
remedy: For interface/address queries use getifaddrs() (declared in <ifaddrs.h>, links with -lsocket in SDP 8.0 build 141). AF_ROUTE/PF_ROUTE are defined in the SDP: evaluate a routing socket for routing-table changes (not tested).
verify: Header/link probes on SDP 8.0 build 141; sockets not run.

positive:
s = socket(AF_NETLINK, SOCK_RAW, NETLINK_ROUTE);
struct sockaddr_nl sa;

present.message: AF_NETLINK/PF_NETLINK are defined in the SDP headers, but struct sockaddr_nl and the NETLINK_* protocol numbers are not: netlink is not usable. Defined-ness of a macro does not mean the family is supported.

title: Linux-specific socket options
message: Socket options that originated on Linux. On SDP 8.0 build 141: TCP_FASTOPEN, TCP_INFO, TCP_NODELAY, TCP_KEEPIDLE/INTVL/CNT, SO_REUSEPORT are defined; TCP_CORK, TCP_QUICKACK, TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT, TCP_USER_TIMEOUT, MSG_MORE, SO_BINDTODEVICE, SO_PRIORITY, SO_MARK, IP_PKTINFO-style Linux options are not.
remedy: Guard each setsockopt/getsockopt with #ifdef so it compiles away when the macro is undefined. Where the macro IS defined (TCP_INFO, TCP_FASTOPEN, SO_REUSEPORT) the struct layout and semantics are BSD's and were not tested: confirm before relying on a same-named constant.
verify: Macro presence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (compile probe); semantics not run.

positive:
setsockopt(s, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_CORK, &on, 4);
setsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEPORT, &on, 4);

present.message: Defined in the SDP headers (compile probe only). The struct layout/semantics follow the BSD-derived stack and were not tested.

title: SO_PEERCRED / struct ucred
message: SO_PEERCRED / struct ucred are Linux-specific in this form: neither exists in SDP 8.0 build 141 user headers.
remedy: Use getpeereid(fd, &uid, &gid) (declared in <unistd.h>, exported by libsocket in SDP 8.0 build 141: link -lsocket) or getsockopt(fd, 0, LOCAL_PEERCRED, &xucred, ...) (LOCAL_PEERCRED is defined in <sys/un.h>, struct xucred in <sys/ucred.h>); behaviour not run on a target. MsgReceive's _msg_info only applies if the design moves to native QNX message passing.
verify: Names verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; semantics not run.

positive:
getsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_PEERCRED, &c, &l);
struct ucred cr;

title: Linux-only open() flags
message: These open() flags originated on Linux. None of O_PATH, O_TMPFILE, O_NOATIME, O_DIRECT is defined in SDP 8.0 build 141.
remedy: Drop or emulate: O_TMPFILE -> mkstemp()+unlink(); O_PATH -> open(O_RDONLY) is not equivalent (symlink handling and permission checks differ), so check what the caller needs; O_NOATIME -> omit; O_DIRECT -> omit (the SDP defines no such flag).
verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

positive:
fd = open(p, O_TMPFILE|O_RDWR, 0600);
fd = open(p, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECT);

title: Linux-only fcntl commands
message: fcntl commands that are Linux extensions. None of F_SETPIPE_SZ/GETPIPE_SZ, F_OFD_*, F_ADD_SEALS/GET_SEALS, F_SETLEASE/GETLEASE, F_SETSIG is defined in SDP 8.0 build 141.
remedy: Guard with #ifdef; for pipe size tuning there is no assumed equivalent, accept the default.
verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: getauxval
message: Auxiliary vector access is Linux/glibc-specific. On SDP 8.0 build 141 <sys/auxv.h> exists but getauxval is not declared or exported (elf_aux_info is absent too).
remedy: Use compile-time feature macros, or QNX's system page (SYSPAGE_ENTRY(cpuinfo)->flags) for CPU feature bits.
verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: sysinfo()
message: Linux sysinfo structure/call (memory, uptime, load). Neither the call nor struct sysinfo exists in SDP 8.0 build 141 (no <sys/sysinfo.h>).
remedy: Use sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) and sysconf(_SC_PHYS_PAGES)/_SC_AVPHYS_PAGES (all three names are defined in SDP 8.0 build 141; what values they return on a target was not tested); uptime from clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC); the QNX system page (<sys/syspage.h>, SYSPAGE_ENTRY and asinfo) is the usual source for memory facts, so check there as well.
verify: Absence and macro names verified on SDP 8.0 build 141; return values not run.

title: mremap / Linux mmap flags
message: mremap and these mmap flags are Linux-specific. mremap, MAP_POPULATE, MAP_HUGETLB and MAP_GROWSDOWN do not exist in SDP 8.0 build 141.
remedy: Replace mremap by mmap new + copy/munmap old (or reserve address space up front); drop MAP_POPULATE/HUGETLB hints.

positive:
p = mremap(a, o, n, MREMAP_MAYMOVE);
mmap(0, n, 3, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_POPULATE, fd, 0);

verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: Linux/glibc non-portable pthread calls
message: glibc _np extensions. On SDP 8.0 build 141 pthread_getattr_np, pthread_tryjoin_np, pthread_timedjoin_np and pthread_yield do not exist (pthread_setname_np and pthread_getname_np do, and are not matched by this rule).
remedy: pthread_yield -> sched_yield(); tryjoin/timedjoin -> a completion flag + condition variable with timed wait.
verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: Linux-only clock ids
message: Clock ids that are Linux extensions. CLOCK_BOOTTIME, CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW, CLOCK_*_COARSE, CLOCK_TAI and the *_ALARM ids are not defined in SDP 8.0 build 141; CLOCK_MONOTONIC and CLOCK_REALTIME are.
remedy: Use CLOCK_MONOTONIC / CLOCK_REALTIME; keep the Linux ids behind #ifdef CLOCK_BOOTTIME.
verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: Linux-only scheduling policies
message: Linux scheduling policies. SCHED_BATCH, SCHED_IDLE and SCHED_DEADLINE are not defined in SDP 8.0 build 141; SCHED_OTHER, SCHED_FIFO, SCHED_RR and SCHED_SPORADIC are.
remedy: Use pthread_setschedparam() with SCHED_RR/SCHED_FIFO and choose priorities for the QNX range; nice values do not map directly.
verify: Verified absent on SDP 8.0 build 141.

title: System V IPC
message: System V IPC is not usable on QNX 8.0 (SDP build 141): shmget/shmat/shmctl/semget/semop/semctl are not declared (sys/sem.h has them in a commented-out 'not currently supported' block; there is no sys/shm.h), and msgget/msgsnd/msgrcv/msgctl are named in <sys/msg.h> but not visible to the compiler.
remedy: POSIX shm_open()/sem_open()/mq_open() for a quick port; for a request/reply design use native message passing (ChannelCreate/ConnectAttach, MsgSend/MsgReceive/MsgReply).
verify: Verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (header text and probes).

title: FUSE filesystem
message: FUSE is a Linux kernel facility.
remedy: The QNX counterpart of a user-space filesystem/device is a resource manager: resmgr_attach(), iofunc_*, dispatch_create()/dispatch_block(). Map each fuse_operations callback to an io_* handler.
refs: QNX docs: Writing a Resource Manager

positive:
fuse_main(argc, argv, &ops, NULL);
struct fuse_operations ops;

title: Linux device node paths
message: Device paths are served by drivers; Linux names will not exist on QNX.
remedy: Take the device path from configuration and implement a QNX default; QNX devices are published by resource managers (for example UART ports appear as /dev/ser1, /dev/ser2).
verify: verify against SDP/BSP: the actual path for each peripheral on the target board.

title: Linux-only preprocessor branch without QNX branch
message: A Linux conditional on this line does not mention QNX. QNX compilers predefine __QNXNTO__ (and __QNX__).
remedy: Add an explicit #elif defined(__QNXNTO__) branch, or widen the condition if the code is POSIX-generic.

title: UNIX-domain socket IPC
message: Likely works unchanged (POSIX), listed because request/reply IPC is where QNX native message passing pays off.
remedy: First port as-is. If this is a hot request/reply path, consider ChannelCreate()/MsgSend()/MsgReceive()/MsgReply(); it gives priority inheritance across the call.
verify: verify against SDP: abstract-namespace sockets (leading NUL in sun_path) are Linux-only.

positive:
struct sockaddr_un a;
s = socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0);

title: /proc/self/exe
message: The Linux /proc/<pid>/exe symlink is not a QNX interface.
remedy: Use _cmdname() to get the running program's path.
verify: verify against SDP: _cmdname() semantics (may return argv[0]-derived path).

title: Linux /proc paths
message: QNX has a /proc, but it is a different interface (process address spaces, not Linux text files).
remedy: Replace with POSIX/QNX queries: sysconf(), getrusage(), the system page (<sys/syspage.h>) for CPU/memory facts, procfs devctl calls for process info. /proc/self/maps has no file equivalent: open /proc/self/as and use devctl(fd, DCMD_PROC_MAPINFO, ...) (and DCMD_PROC_INFO for the process summary), both defined in <sys/procfs.h> in SDP 8.0 build 141; the structure layout and calls were not run.
verify: DCMD_PROC_MAPINFO / DCMD_PROC_INFO and <sys/procfs.h> verified present on SDP 8.0 build 141 (probes); procfs layout and devctl usage not run on a target.

title: Linux /sys (sysfs) paths
message: sysfs is a Linux kernel pseudo-filesystem; not assumed on QNX.
remedy: Query the real source: sysconf/getifaddrs for system facts, device resource managers for hardware state, the system page for CPU data.

title: /dev/shm
message: On QNX POSIX shared memory objects appear under /dev/shmem, not /dev/shm.
remedy: Use shm_open("/name", ...) and let the system pick the namespace instead of hard-coding the directory.

title: Includes <endian.h>, <sys/endian.h> or <byteswap.h>
message: <endian.h>, <sys/endian.h> and <byteswap.h> do not exist in the QNX 8.0 SDP (build 141). Code that includes one without a QNX branch stops at the include (iperf's portable_endian.h falls into its 'platform not supported' branch and includes <endian.h>).
remedy: Byte-order conversion is in <net/netbyte.h> (pulled in by <netinet/in.h>): htole16/32/64, le16/32/64toh, htobe16/32/64 and be16/32/64toh are macros there (present in build 141); <gulliver.h> has ENDIAN_LE16/32 and ENDIAN_BE16/32; BYTE_ORDER and BIG_ENDIAN come from <sys/param.h>. There is no bswap_16/32/64 and no __BYTE_ORDER / __LITTLE_ENDIAN. Add a __QNXNTO__ branch that includes <net/netbyte.h> and <sys/param.h>.
verify: Header absence and the macro names verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (qcc probes); not run on a target.

title: glibc bswap_N byte-swap helpers
message: bswap_16/32/64 are glibc <byteswap.h> helpers. On the QNX 8.0 SDP (build 141) they are undeclared (and <byteswap.h> does not exist).
remedy: Use the htole*/htobe*/le*toh/be*toh macros from <net/netbyte.h> (present in build 141) or ENDIAN_LE32()/ENDIAN_BE32() from <gulliver.h> instead of bswap_N. Do not redeclare htole64 and friends as functions: on QNX they are macros and the redeclaration fails to compile (dropbear's compat.h).
verify: Name absence and the replacement names verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (probes); not run on a target.

title: POLLRDHUP
message: POLLRDHUP (peer shut down its writing half) is Linux-specific. It is not defined in the QNX 8.0 SDP (build 141).
remedy: Detect a peer's close by reading: POLLIN, then read()/recv() returning 0 means orderly shutdown; POLLHUP, POLLPRI and POLLRDNORM are defined in <poll.h> (build 141). Whether POLLHUP is raised for a half-close on QNX sockets was not tested, so keep the read()==0 path as the authority.
verify: Absence of POLLRDHUP and presence of POLLHUP verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (probes); half-close behaviour not run on a target.

title: Real-time signals (SIGRTMIN, SIGRTMAX)
message: SIGRTMIN and SIGRTMAX are used for real-time signals. They are defined in the QNX 8.0 SDP (build 141, <signal.h>), as are sigqueue, sigtimedwait and sigwaitinfo.
remedy: Defined-ness is not parity: check how many real-time signals QNX provides against the highest SIGRTMIN+N the code uses, that sigqueue() delivery and queueing match what the code relies on, and that signal numbers are not assumed identical to Linux's (glibc reserves the first ones for threads). On QNX a pulse (SIGEV_PULSE, MsgSendPulse) is the native event.
verify: Macro and function presence verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (probes); the number of real-time signals and delivery semantics not checked or run.

present.message: SIGRTMIN/SIGRTMAX are defined in the SDP headers (signal.h) and sigqueue, sigtimedwait and sigwaitinfo link. The number of real-time signals and their delivery semantics were not compared with Linux.

title: glibc byte-order macros (__BYTE_ORDER, __LITTLE_ENDIAN)
message: __BYTE_ORDER and __LITTLE_ENDIAN are glibc macros: on the QNX 8.0 SDP (build 141) __BYTE_ORDER is undeclared and __LITTLE_ENDIAN is in no user header. In an #if both evaluate to 0, so '#if __BYTE_ORDER == __LITTLE_ENDIAN' is silently TRUE on QNX whatever the CPU's order.
remedy: Use BYTE_ORDER with LITTLE_ENDIAN / BIG_ENDIAN from <sys/param.h> (present in build 141), or the ENDIAN_* macros of <gulliver.h>; both x86_64 and aarch64le targets are little-endian, so a wrong branch would corrupt data without a compile error.
verify: Macro absence and the replacement names verified on SDP 8.0 build 141 (probes); not run on a target.
